query: Why does excluding a dependency via optimizeDeps.exclude break JSX-runtime exports when a route is lazy loaded?
reference_answer:
> The excluded ESM package dynamically imports `react-tiny-popover`, whose published entry is CommonJS; because that nested dependency is not discovered during the initial crawl, it is served unbundled and fails at runtime. Adding `optimizeDeps: { include: ['internal-ui > react-tiny-popover'] }` fixes the reproduction. Vite's docs already call out including nested CommonJS dependencies of excluded ESM packages: https://vite.dev/config/dep-optimization-options.html#optimizedeps-exclude. I don't think this needs a Vite code change unless the report still reproduces with that nested dependency included.

Yep, this is correct.

query: Why do CSS url() references stay unchanged after PostCSS processing in Vite 8.2.x?
reference_answer:
> The regression reproduces in two independent configurations:

This isn't true.`vite.tailwind.config.mjs` has `css.postcss: path.resolve(reproRoot, 'postcss.empty.cjs')` which will load `postcss.config.mjs` as that option specifies the directory that the config is searched from, not the config path. If you set `css.postcss: {}`, it doesn't reproduce.

Checking the code in the wild, I think Vite's code aligns with them and it should be fixed on the `postcss-lightningcss` side.

If you print out `chunk.code`, you can actually see that `assets/search-xxx.js` actually exists at that point and is imported by other chunks. The removal is done by [this code](https://github.com/vitejs/vite/blob/a07a4bd052ac75f916391c999c408ad5f2867e61/packages/vite/src/node/plugins/css.ts#L1051-L1128).

query: Why does importing a type with the inline `type` modifier in v8 pull in unused dependencies, when a separate `import type` statement does not, unlike in v7?

When that option is enabled, `import { type SomeType } from './ReproModule'` is transformed to `import './ReproModule'` (`import type { SomeType } from './ReproModule'` is removed regardless of that option).

It has the same behavior in v7 as well: https://stackblitz.com/edit/github-r2xs21wm?file=src%2FIssueComponent.tsx&terminal=build
(`" (see https://github.com/apollographql/invariant-packages)"` that comes from `ts-invariant` exists in `dist/index-hash.js`)

query: Why does the code returned from the generateBundle hook in Rollup v8 have its directives, comments, and unused variables removed?
reference_answer:
Rollup docs does not explain what value `RenderedModule.code` contains. But from the name and the implementation ([code](https://github.com/rollup/rollup/blob/186b352f3b028c5733c47dadacd565e303567e9d/src/Chunk.ts#L1350-L1384)), I think it should return the code after the treeshaking was applied. So I think it is expected to be removed if the variable is not used. In fact, Rollup seems to remove the unused variables and the directives ([tweaked stackblitz with Vite 7](https://stackblitz.com/edit/github-dmwtfi2p?file=vite.config.ts,package.json,node_modules%2F.pnpm%2Frollup%404.60.1%2Fnode_modules%2Frollup%2Fdist%2Frollup.d.ts)).

Rollup also seems to remove the comment if the adjacent code is removed (see the stackblitz example linked above). On the other hand, Rolldown removes comments other than the ones listed [here](https://rolldown.rs/reference/OutputOptions.comments) and Vite disables all of these when minify is enabled (i.e. all comments will be removed). If you turn them on, it will be included in the output, which I guess is not desired. Even if Rolldown aligned the comments behavior with Rollup, it won't work in some cases as the comment will be removed if the adjacent code is removed.

If it works, I think it would be safer to inject a function call instead of a comment (e.g. `astroHeadInject()`) and remove that call in `renderChunk`.
query_title: [v8] The hook `generateBundle` returns code stripped of directives, comments and unused variables

If you replace

```ts
import.meta.glob("./!(stories|types|Common|lib|const|admin-ui)/*!(spec|test|stories).tsx")
```
with
```ts
import.meta.glob([
  "./**/*.tsx",
  "!./{stories,types,Common,lib,const,admin-ui}/**/*.tsx",
  "!./**/*.{spec,test,stories}.tsx",
])
```
it should work the same.

We'll track the extglob support at https://github.com/vitejs/vite/issues/21947

query: Why does Vite 7.2.x remove comments that start with an exclamation mark?
reference_answer:
`/*! */` is treated as legal comments by most tools, and it isn't a way to mark "important" as purgecss docs mentioned. So it relying on that behavior isn't really robust if people want to strip away legal comments if they plan to handle it externally.

The proper way around this I suppose is to ensure purgecss runs before we minify with esbuild (which is removing the legal comments), which should be the case if you're configuring purgecss through postcss, however I don't see it in the setup. Or if purgecss has to run after esbuild minifies/processes, then esbuild (and every tool) needs to handle the special comment, just like how they have special code paths for preserving `/* webpackChunkName */` and `/* @vite-ignore */` in JS.
query_title: Vite 7.2.x strips bang comments

query: How can I set where the lock file is stored to resolve problems with the dependency optimizer?
reference_answer:
Vite checks the internal lockfile that represents the current state of the `node_modules` (`./node_modules/.pnpm/lock.yaml` for pnpm). This is slightly different from the normal lockfile (`./pnpm.lock`). Even if Vite exposed the option, I'm not sure if Vite or the monorepo tool can have a proper document about this.
Instead of a normal option, Vite can add a special env var that is meant to be set by the monorepo tool. But I'm not sure if that's worth as I'm not aware of other tools moving the path of the lock files.
As an alternative, I think we can add
```js
{
  path: '.rush/temp/shrinkwrap-deps.json',
  // Included in lockfile
  checkPatchesDir: false,
  manager: 'pnpm',
},
```
to
https://github.com/vitejs/vite/blob/925cefe8ee5c88c9b5b6fa525f46addc4a8aef83/packages/vite/src/node/optimizer/index.ts#L1236-L1241
.
query_title: Configuration for lock file location to fix issues with dependency optimizer

Looks like right now the generated sourcemap by rollup skips over that and the `e=JSON.parse(...),` part gets included with the previous mapping.

Maybe worth checking if this is the case in a plain rollup setup.

query: Why did npm take down a Stylus package for containing malicious code?
reference_answer:
It declares the additional dependencies that vite can import, and the versions that Vite supports. In a strict installation, packages can only import the declared deps and peer deps. You can't import some arbitrary dep, and if it somehow works, potentially getting the wrong version. An optional peer deps means additionally package managers don't have to install it and vite can function normally with it not installed, until the user manually installs it.

I'd suggest reading some resources/docs on how optional peer deps work.
query_title: Stylus package was removed by npm for malicious code

query: Why does Vite keep serving an old build of my local library even after I restart the dev server?
reference_answer:
Vite does not re-run the optimizer if the lock file did not change. (because checking the actual files requires crawling the files and would be slow)
https://github.com/vitejs/vite/blob/f530a72246ec8e73b1f2ba767f6c108e9ac9712a/packages/vite/src/node/optimizer/index.ts#L379-L403
Normally the dependency file only changes when the lock file changed or if it's a symlink to somewhere else. For symlink cases, Vite excludes the symlinks from the optimizer by default, so it isn't a problem.

In your case (npm `file:` + `--install-links`), the dependency files changes without the lockfile being changed even though it's not a symlink.
If removing `--install-links` works fine, I'd recommend that. If not, maybe using a package manager that updates the lock file when the content changes could solve your problem (I'm not sure if there're any though).
query_title: Vite serves an outdated version of local library after a restart

query: What should the default value of build.target be set to in the current version?

In the last meeting, we concluded that it would be nice to align with [Baseline](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Glossary/Baseline/Compatibility).

For each major version, Vite will update the default `build.target` to the browser list used to generate "Baseline Widely available" (the browsers released at least 2.5 years ago).
For example, if Vite 7 were released in May 2025, the default `build.target` will be:
- Safari 15.6
- Chrome 104
- Edge 104
- Firefox 104

query: How can I fix bundling failures when deploying Prisma with serverless functions?
reference_answer:
More simple reproduction: https://stackblitz.com/edit/github-jxnpwg49?file=server%2Fapp.ts,vite.config.ts,package.json&terminal=build (needs to run locally as prisma does not work in stackblitz)

It seems prisma generates `node_modules/.prisma/client` and imports that from `node_modules/@prisma/client/default.js` by `require('.prisma/client/default')`.
While `require('.prisma/client/default')` works, Vite does not support that because it's not supported for imports (i.e. `import '.prisma/client/default'` errors with `ERR_INVALID_MODULE_SPECIFIER` ([spec](https://nodejs.org/api/esm.html#resolution-and-loading-algorithm:~:text=If%20packageName%20starts,Module%20Specifier%20error.)). Technically, Vite should allow that to be resolved for `require`, but I think it's better to be avoided and the default generated location should be changed on prisma side.

For a workaround, you can change the location.
https://www.prisma.io/docs/orm/prisma-client/setup-and-configuration/generating-prisma-client#the-location-of-prisma-client
For example, update `schema.prisma` to include the following code:
```
generator client {
  provider = "prisma-client-js"
  output = "../node_modules/@prisma/client-generated"
}
```
and update the import to use `@prisma/client-generated` (instead of `@prisma/client`).
query_title: Unable to bundle Prisma for serverless functions
